jobs.title: Vice President, Enterprise Services
jobs.location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
jobs.description:
WorkplaceNL
administers Newfoundland and Labrador’s mandatory, no-fault workplace injury compensation system, funded by employer assessments and investment returns. We promote safe workplaces and provide benefits and services to injured workers, helping improve quality of life across the province.

Overview

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Enterprise Services brings an organization-wide perspective to strategy, performance, technology, people and enterprise risk.
This position provides executive leadership and strategic direction for Enterprise Services and is integral to WorkplaceNL’s modernization agenda, working in partnership with those leading transformation initiatives to ensure improvements are effectively integrated into ongoing operations. This is a long term temporary position, anticipated to span several years while WorkplaceNL advances its transformation and modernization program.

As a member of the Executive Team, you will help set WorkplaceNL’s direction and align people, resources and investments behind shared priorities. Your mandate extends beyond leading your portfolio: you will work across organizational boundaries, navigate competing needs and build support for changes that strengthen services and organizational performance.

You will also lead the continued development of WorkplaceNL’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework and report to the Board’s Governance Committee.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategy and planning:
Working with the Executive Team and senior leaders to translate long-term priorities into evidence-based, multi-year plans with clear accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

Technology and information management:
Guiding technology investments, budgets and service delivery to support organizational priorities. Overseeing information management, cybersecurity and business resilience, and advising senior leaders and the Board on technology opportunities and risks.

Performance and improvement:
Leading corporate performance measurement, reporting and continuous improvement. Overseeing Internal Review, program evaluation and quality assurance, and guiding compliance with the Transparency and Accountability Act, annual performance reporting and CEO performance contracts.

Policy and government relations:
Guiding the policy framework and annual policy plan, overseeing statutory reviews and legislative priorities, and maintaining productive relationships with government and other stakeholders.

People and culture:
Setting the context for HR strategies that support employee health and safety, engagement, recruitment, retention and succession. Working with leaders to strengthen organizational capability and foster an ethical, inclusive and accountable workplace.

Enterprise risk:
Strengthening risk management across the organization, ensuring risks inform planning, investment and operational decisions, with clear reporting to the Executive Team and Board.

Who you are

You lead with an enterprise perspective, making decisions based on what serves the organization as a whole. You build trust across functions and understand the people dynamics that shape organizational performance. You can surface competing interests, work through disagreement and bring people together around a clear direction. Where delivery relies on shared resources, you help leaders make sound trade-offs, establish priorities and agree on how work will move forward.
You are comfortable leading change and transformation through influence, ingenuity as well as authority. You communicate the reasons for change clearly, build commitment and maintain accountability for results. You develop strong leaders, address concerns directly and create the conditions for teams to work effectively together.

You bring sound judgement and executive presence to discussions with the CEO, Board, government, and other stakeholders. You can explain complex issues clearly, offer candid advice and connect operational decisions to strategy, risk, financial stewardship and client service.

What you bring:

A university degree in business, public administration, humanities, science or relevant disciplines. A master’s degree in a relevant discipline would be considered an asset.
Minimum of ten years of progressive management experience in a public or private organization leading multiple lines of business and providing services to diverse client groups.
Demonstrated ability to navigate a public sector environment, balancing government priorities, board oversight, public accountability and organizational objectives.
Strong leadership abilities with exceptional interpersonal and communication skills and a proven track record of building effective stakeholder relationships.
Experience conceptualizing and executing strategies that advance cross-organizational priorities, including in the areas of information technology, data and analytics.
Experience applying best practices in enterprise risk management.
Experience with project planning, management and governance, especially as it relates to information technology.
Ability to think strategically, analytically, and use good judgement in providing oversight and solutions to corporate opportunities, challenges and risks.

Why Join Us?
Impactful work that contributes to the work safety in Newfoundland and Labrador.
Competitive base salary; range $126,040 - $163,852
Generous vacation and leave entitlements.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits.
Enrollment in the Public Service Pension Plan.
Opportunities for ongoing professional development.
A collaborative, supportive, and inclusive work environment.

At Workplace NL we are committed to workplace inclusion. Candidates of all backgrounds including but not limited to individuals with international experience, newcomers to Canada, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, members of visible minorities, and persons of various gender identities and sexual orientations are encouraged to apply. We welcome the opportunity to discuss accommodation at any point in the application process.

If you require reasonable accommodation to take part in the employment process, please call 709-437-4300 or send an email to recruitment@ethree.ca and let us know the nature of your request.
We thank all applicants for their interest. However, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Director of Sales, Enterprise
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Sales, Enterprise based in Canada.

The Director of Sales, Enterprise will lead enterprise revenue growth across North America, driving new business acquisition and expanding relationships with strategic customers. This leadership role combines sales strategy, team development, and hands-on involvement in complex, high-value SaaS transactions. You will manage and coach a team of Account Executives while building a predictable, scalable enterprise sales engine. Working closely with senior executives and cross-functional teams, you will strengthen go-to-market execution and expand the organization's presence in the Life Sciences sector. The role requires strong commercial judgment, executive relationship-building skills, and the ability to navigate lengthy, multi-stakeholder sales cycles. You will help shape enterprise sales performance in a fast-growing, innovative software environment.

Accountabilities

Drive enterprise revenue growth: Own and execute the North American enterprise sales strategy, achieving new business annual recurring revenue (ARR) targets and expanding market share across strategic accounts.
Develop sales strategy: Establish structured approaches for complex enterprise sales cycles, including account planning, opportunity qualification, stakeholder mapping, and deal execution.
Lead and develop the sales team: Manage, mentor, and coach Account Executives through hands-on guidance, performance management, and ongoing professional development.
Support strategic deals: Engage directly in high-value opportunities, helping the team develop deal strategies, build executive relationships, navigate procurement, negotiate commercial terms, and close business.
Build executive relationships: Develop and maintain relationships with senior decision-makers across pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device organizations in the United States and Canada.
Manage pipeline and performance: Maintain a healthy enterprise pipeline, monitor sales metrics, and identify ways to improve conversion rates, deal progression, and overall sales effectiveness.
Expand market opportunities: Identify and pursue new enterprise accounts across North America, developing targeted strategies and strengthening market positioning within the Life Sciences industry.
Collaborate across departments: Work closely with Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Revenue Operations to align go-to-market initiatives and address complex customer needs.
Oversee forecasting and reporting: Lead pipeline reviews, revenue forecasting, and sales reporting, providing senior leadership with visibility into opportunities, risks, and expected performance.

Requirements

8+ years of experience in B2B SaaS sales, with a focus on enterprise accounts.
At least 3 years of experience in sales management or leadership, including managing, coaching, and developing Account Executives.
Proven record of achieving and exceeding enterprise sales targets in North American and global markets, including closing complex, high-value SaaS deals.
Experience selling SaaS solutions to Life Sciences organizations or within Quality Management, Compliance, or other highly regulated industries.
Strong understanding of the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device sectors, including international regulatory and compliance requirements such as FDA, EMA, and GxP.
Extensive knowledge of complex enterprise sales cycles, including multi-stakeholder decision-making, executive-level engagement, procurement, and contract negotiations.
Strong business acumen and the ability to communicate technical capabilities in terms of measurable business value to C-level executives and senior decision-makers.
Hands-on leadership approach, with the ability to guide teams through discovery, qualification, value-based selling, negotiation, and closing.
Strong analytical skills and experience with revenue forecasting, pipeline management, and sales performance metrics.
Ability to balance strategic planning with direct sales involvement in a dynamic, fast-growing environment.
Availability to work primarily Eastern Time (ET) hours to collaborate effectively with internal teams.
Nice to have: Experience selling Quality Management Systems (QMS) or compliance software; experience scaling enterprise sales teams and processes in early- to mid-stage SaaS companies; familiarity with Salesforce-native SaaS products and go-to-market environments.

Benefits

The source job posting does not specify a salary range or detailed benefits package.
Full-time position with a remote work arrangement across North America.
Opportunity to lead enterprise sales strategy and develop a high-performing Account Executive team.
Exposure to strategic customers in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries.
Opportunity to contribute to the growth of innovative cloud-based SaaS solutions in the Life Sciences sector.
Inclusive work environment committed to equal opportunity and diversity.

How Jobgether Works

We use an AI-powered matching process
to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!

Why Apply Through Jobgether?

Data Privacy Notice:
By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Jobgether will process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy and share relevant information with the hiring employer. This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
